newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes edge up, buyers withdraw.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes edge up, buyers withdraw.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices edged up with national benchmark grades early Monday, while discounts were unchanged as traders held off buying for next month, traders said.
"It's still early for June deals," one refinery buyer said.
Traders heard Texaco offered to sell at least one 350,000-barrel cargo of Oriente crude priced off June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI).
The crude had been offered earlier for April delivery, and was priced off May WTI.
Oriente crude can be used in place of Alaska North Slope (ANS), a staple of West Coast refineries.
Outright prices for ANS crude rose five cents Monday to $18.43/18.63 a barrel, with the last deal done two weeks ago at $1.32 under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude.
BP, the crude's main producer, priced their barrels at $1.15 under WTI, buyers said.
"It's still not a realistic offer. There are foreign alternatives that are a better price," said a buyer for a small refinery.
On a notional basis, Line 63 was talked $2.37/2.27 under May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI). The grade rarely trades off WTI.
Traders reported no deals in Line 63 and heavy California grades.
